title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations on the loop equation' continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck studies an automorphism of the profinite group π̂_{0,3}, i.e. a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type element. It is given by a 'cyclotomic' parameter μ ∈ Ẑ* and a 'twisting' element. He follows its image under the abelianisation-type homomorphism N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), the action on H_1 of the once-punctured elliptic curve.

Notation. Everything is written in 2×2 matrices over Ẑ:
- σ_∞ is the involution (order 2), and ρ is the order-3 rotation acting on the elements.
- l_0 = (1 2;0 1) and l_1 = (1 0;2 1) are the images of the standard generators. These are squares of the elementary matrices, since the level-2 congruence subgroup is free on them.
- f = (r s; t u) has det f = ru − st = 1.
- α_0 = (a b; c d), and ξ = l_0^ν α_0, where ν is linked to μ.

Relations used. From the earlier formulas (45), (56):
- the loop equation g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = ε;
- g = ε α ρ(α)^{-1}.
The previous page proved ε = ε_2(μ) (μ mod 4) and δ = det α_0 = ε_3(μ) (μ mod 3).

Computation. He sets α = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} α_0 and computes two things:
- α explicitly as f^{-1} l_0^ν α_0 (formula 64). This mixes r,s,t,u with a,b,c,d.
- g = ᵗf · l_1^ν · ρ(f), using σ_∞(f^{-1}) = ᵗf and the formula for ρ(f) from §43 (77).

The result is (65): g = (1+μt(t+u), −μt²; −1+μu(t+u), 1−μut).
- This depends only on f (and μ), not on α_0 or ξ.
- The margin note stresses the point: unlike α_0, ᵗf, ξ and φ, the element g is determined without ambiguity.

What comes next. The page closes by proposing a notation that identifies elements of π̂_{0,3} and Ĝ_{0,3} with their images in GL(2,Ẑ). The next page uses it to seek a canonical u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) with det u = μ inducing the given automorphism on SL(2,Ẑ)'. Such a u is unique only up to ±1 at each prime.

Purpose. Compute explicitly the linear (abelianised, genus-1) shadow of a GT-type automorphism and find a canonical matrix representative.
errors: No mathematical error found. Check: det(65) = 1 identically, using ru − st = 1.

Back-solving from the final product, the middle factor l_1^ν ρ(f) must be (t+u, −t; μ(t+u) − r − s, r − μt). With this, all four entries of (65) follow from ru − st = 1. The transcription's partially struck entries are consistent with this.

ideas.what: Explicit matrix image in GL(2,Ẑ) (via the action on H_1 of π̂_{1,1}) of a solution of the loop equation g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = ε for a GT-type automorphism with cyclotomic parameter μ
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT (or of Gal(Q̄/Q)) in GL_2(Ẑ) via the abelianisation of π̂_1 of the once-punctured elliptic curve, M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara (GT); Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps for genus-1 extensions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the role of M_{1,1} and the 'Teichmüller tower'; no such computations appear there

ideas.what: Observation that g is canonical (depends only on f and μ) while α, ξ and α_0 involve choices; ambiguity of the lift u up to the 2-torsion of Ẑ*, i.e. {±1}^P
ideas.modern_name: Canonical lifting of an outer action to GL_2 with prescribed determinant (cyclotomic character)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit matrix computation within Grothendieck's private GT/loop-equation calculations. The result is correct and consistent, but it is elementary bookkeeping toward a canonical GL_2(Ẑ) representative, not a new idea.
transcription_corrections: Middle factor of the g product should read (t+u, −t; μ(t+u) − r − s, r − μt), i.e. l_1^ν ρ(f). The transcription's '[-...-]' entries and '−μt + [-...-]' correspond to these.
f itself is (r s; t u) with det ru − st = 1, so that f^{-1} = (u −s; −t r) and ᵗf = (r t; s u).

Margin note reads roughly: 'NB Contrairement à α_0, ᵗf, et à ξ, φ qui s'en déduisent, g a l'avantage et l'intérêt d'être déterminé sans ambiguïté par ℓ (connaissant μ), autrement dit ne dépend que de f et du choix fait de ν...'
